### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getLocales (symbol, a method of interface HookRefusalI18nService), /api/v1/i18n/locales (route, the route ledger binds it to client method i18n.getLocales))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via buildSession (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via getLocales (symbol, a method of interface HookRefusalI18nService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via TranslationDataSchema (symbol, a top-level const), globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in PER_APP_SETTINGS_PLATFORM_ONLY))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in PER_APP_SETTINGS_PLATFORM_ONLY))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const), HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const), bindAppArtifactHandlers (symbol, a top-level function), globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/i18n/locales (route, the route ledger binds it to client method i18n.getLocales))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **157** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b5a3ca50e02e346cdf7a26a5083c7f2a9de7706` — the merge of head `e55978368d717b982ea1573917b9f9aea2f9c885` into base `a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b5a3ca50e02e346cdf7a26a5083c7f2a9de7706 && git checkout 8b5a3ca50e02e346cdf7a26a5083c7f2a9de7706
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d e55978368d717b982ea1573917b9f9aea2f9c885 && git checkout -B drift-repro a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d && git merge --no-ff e55978368d717b982ea1573917b9f9aea2f9c885

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a20824f3661810909cfd701c29da1ba04e4a081d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `78dc14528e8a3d403f551ff7500b33e72c984b26`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/references/_index.md, skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, skills/objectstack-platform/references/_index.md + every other path of the 52-file diff outside the prose faces (runtime sandbox hook-refusal-catalogue.ts / body-runner.ts / quickjs-runner.ts / app-plugin.ts / app-artifact-handlers.ts, objectql engine-execution-plumbing.ts, cli i18n-extract.ts / i18n-coverage.ts, lint validate-translation-references.ts, the five test files, the changeset, the ui preview and loader lists, the walk-parity fixture, the metadata-protocol count pin, the ADR-0122 pin, the form-reconciliation ledger, the generated spec artifacts) and the cited code read on main: packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (mapDataError, sandboxBusinessMessage, isSandboxCrash), packages/types/src/native-error-name.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts (REJECT_HANDLER, hostErrorToVm, SandboxError), packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts (locale), packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts (resolveBundleLocale), packages/spec/src/data/hook.form.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts, scripts/check-error-code-casing.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md (the Skills-docs line spelling).

Inputs read: card #26170 body and all 6 comments (decision 6430864109, brief 6431195984, ruling 6431311681 letter A, claim 6442821427, os-dev-report 6449646620); PR #26831 body, 52-path file list, the three-dot diff at this head (merge-base `c8583f80ac`, 52 files +1703/−99, matching), the one PR comment (the docs-drift bot, 6449723825); the head's check-runs read three times, last at 2026-10-27T18:06:53Z. Main has moved 6 commits past the merge-base; the one shared path is translation.zod.ts (main tightened LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE to 2–3 letters in a region disjoint from the new `hooks` group) — a merge is owed before the queue, no semantic conflict read. ⚠️ The PR head moved to `e5ea8881c7` while this review ran (one commit, one line: an `adr0112-ok:` opt-out comment above the `code: 'lower'` fixture in hook-refusals.test.ts); this record judges `78dc1452` as briefed, and says below what the newer head does and does not change.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate readings on this head.** Green: Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate (umbrella), Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected, Check Documentation Links, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · tooling self-tests, Lint · query-options erasure, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source gates, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, filter (21). **Red: `Lint · docs & code guards` (failure, 2026-10-27T18:02:01Z)** — its annotation names the step `Error-code casing guard` (`pnpm check:error-code-casing`, ADR-0112 #4003) as the red gate; the three umbrella jobs `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test UI` then report failure, and every remaining shard (Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI/workspace/consumer/debt, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Lint UI, Lint · PM dispatch-gates) reads **cancelled** — superseded by the push of `e5ea8881`, so this head carries NO measured verdict for tests, type-check or the dispatch gates. The raw job log is behind a blob-storage redirect this container's proxy refuses, so only the annotations were read. Cause read in the diff, not the log: `packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusals.test.ts:136` adds the fixture `"throw Object.assign(new Error('x'), { code: 'lower' });"`, and the guard is textual (`code: 'lowercase'` in any .ts under packages/, strings included; `custom` and `unrecognized_keys` are in its NOT_CODES, so every other hit in the diff is clean). The newer head's `adr0112-ok: reason` line is the opt-out the guard honours (`findViolations` reads it on the line above, counted in the verdict's optOuts); that is a legitimate remedy for a fixture that emits nothing, and leaves EXEMPT_FILES untouched. Skipped: Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood shards, 18.x harness, tarball smoke — all opt-in.

**Ruling A, exactly?** Declaration shape ✓ — `HookSchema.refusals: Record(CODE matching HOOK_REFUSAL_CODE_PATTERN, HookRefusalSchema{ message: trimmed non-empty, status?: int 400–499 })`, closed with aliases (`reason`/`text`/`description` → `message`, `httpStatus`/`statusCode` → `status`) and guidance for `code`/`title`; default 400 lives in the runtime constant `DEFAULT_HOOK_REFUSAL_STATUS`, stated in the describe. Key shape ✓ — `hookRefusalMessageKey` = `hooks.HOOK.refusals.CODE.message`, the `hooks` group on all three translation faces (`appTranslationDataShape` → TranslationData, PlatformTranslationData, TranslationItem), aliases `hook`→`hooks`, `refusal`/`errors`/`messages`→`refusals`, message `optional` so the extract skeleton's empty slot parses. Code-only body ✓ — the existing throw shape is reused (`__errorInfo` carries `code`); no `api.refuse` was added; the body's own text, `status` and `userMessage` are not read. Extract/check ✓ — `walkHookRefusals` emits one `hook`-bucket demand per declared entry (`i18n/missing-hook`), coverage test shows it counts down to zero. Lint ✓ — `translation-target-unknown` over the stack's and sibling artifacts' hooks and their declared codes, nearest-name suggestion. Precedent parity with flow end refusals ✓ (same declaration-keyed posture; by hook name, so `'*'` and multi-object hooks own one catalogue).

**Save-time literal check — sound.** `hookRefusalCodesThrownIn` masks comments and non-code string contents, reads `code: 'X'` inside each `throw` statement's expression and `name.code = 'X'` for a name some `throw` throws bare; SCREAMING_SNAKE literals only; statement ends at `;`/newline outside brackets or the enclosing block close. Misses (helpers, computed codes, template-literal interpolation that unbalances the mask) fall to the runtime refusal, never to silence; its false positives (an `e.code = 'X'` in another scope) refuse toward loud. Guarded on `body.language === 'js'` — an expression body cannot throw a code. Each undeclared code is one issue at `body.source` with the declared list.

**Runtime — loud where the catalogue speaks.** `resolveHookRefusal` returns `err` for no catalogue, a non-SandboxError, no `innerMessage` (the runner's own faults / the engine's relayed refusal), a host-relayed error (`isHostRelayedSandboxError`: the new non-enumerable `[message, code]` marker on every marshalled host error, compared in the VM's reject handler so a body that rewrote either is speaking for itself), a nested relayed refusal, and a native-error crash. A declared code → new `SandboxError(wrapper, message, { code, status: declared ?? 400, userMessage: message })`; `mapDataError` serves 400 → `VALIDATION_ERROR` + `declaredCode`, 409 → `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` + `declaredCode` (the existing demotion contract; tests read it off `mapDataError`). An undeclared code or no code → `new SandboxError(undeclaredHookRefusalAtRun(...))` with no innerMessage → `isSandboxCrash` → `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (ADR-0112 envelope with `code` and `status`, sanitised prose); the hook name, thrown code and declared list reach the server log at `error` through `logBodyThrow` (status ≥ 500 branch). Honest, and the author's fix text is in the log, not on the wire — consistent with the fault posture. The documented spelling `throw Object.assign(new Error(), { code })` with an EMPTY message was checked against the runner: `__error` = `String(e)` = `Error`, `userFacingMessage('Error')` = `Error`, and `NATIVE_ERROR_NAME_RE` deliberately excludes plain `Error`, so it is a business message and the catalogue answers it ✓. An empty `refusals: {}` turns every throw into the 500 fault — loud and consistent.

**Translation and locale — fail-safe.** `declaredRefusalMessage`: no locale / no service / service throws (warned) / key echoed / blank → declared message. `negotiatedLocale` uses `resolveBundleLocale` against `getLocales()` (exact, case-fold, base, variant; `zh` → `zh-CN` tested) and falls back to the requested tag, where `t` echoes the key and the declared message is served — an unknown locale cannot blank or fault the refusal. `buildSession` copies `ExecutionContext.locale` onto a session only AFTER the presence test (a locale alone makes no caller); `ExecutionContext.locale` is Accept-Language first, else the `localization` setting (read in execution-context.zod.ts), which is what the new `session.locale` describe says. This producer is the ruling's "caller's locale" made reachable, not a behaviour beyond the card; descriptive only, no authorization input.

**No params — extensible later, with one caveat.** The declared `message` is plain text "translated whole", stated in the schema describe, the docs and the skill; the catalogue in the ruling has no param slot either, so shipping without one is inside letter A. A later `params` on the thrown error plus holes in the message is additive — EXCEPT that a double-brace sequence written in a message today is served literally and refused nowhere, so a future interpolation would change that string's meaning (a `semantic` kind, not `added`). The widening card should either refuse double-brace holes at the schema now or commit to literal-forever; flagged in ③, not a FAIL.

**Off-surface files — each necessary, none creep.** objectql `buildSession` (the only producer of the caller's locale on the hook session; 3-case test); runtime `app-plugin.ts` ×2 and `app-artifact-handlers.ts` (hand the lazy i18n reader to both bind doors — the default runner and the artifact binder — read at refusal time so a late-registered service is found); ui `TranslationPreview` category + en/zh labels + `SPEC_TRANSLATION_GROUPS` (exhaustive over the groups; the `2/15 (13%)` test update follows from the count); i18n docs (owed by the ruling); walk-parity fixture (authors one hook with a catalogue so the group is walked); `CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS.hook` 22→23 (the pin counts top-level HookSchema keys); ADR-0122 pin 796→797 (`HookRefusalSchema` has no default or transform, so input ≡ output — correctly isomorphic); form-reconciliation ledger omit entry (below). Generated artifacts move consistently: liveness `hook.refusals` (+`message`/`status` children) and `translation.hooks` drilled to `refusals.message`, all `live` with the reader cited; state-counts 21→23 / 38→39; api-surface, authorable-surface, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema manifest, references docs (1556→1557 schemas), strictness-ledger counts 164→165 (one new strictObject in hook.zod) and 384→386 (two in translation.zod) — all match the diff.

**Studio hook form.** `refusals` is not offered; the ledger entry is accurate (the `record` control stamps `keyField` into each entry and `HookRefusalSchema` is closed, so a stamped key is refused). The form DOES offer a `body.source` code field, so a Studio-authored hook has no catalogue and stays on the unchanged branch — not a silent path. It is a declared-but-unofferable gap whose follow-up (a key-only record control) is "noted, not filed" in the dev report; the seat should carry it (③).

**Skills paths — true, with one over-claim read elsewhere.** Both `_index.md` export lists match `hook.zod.ts` at this head. `data-hooks.md`'s new section is true line by line against the code: SCREAMING_SNAKE codes; `declaredCode` on the envelope; translation through the key in the caller's locale; the body's text and status unused; undeclared → save-time if literal else 500; unchanged `ctx.api` errors and crashes pass through; default 400. The deleted handler-based error examples are replaced by one body-based catalogue example and the Testing Hooks section by a reference link; 998→972 lines, under the token ceiling. One claim in the liveness note (not the skill) over-reaches: "the build lowers an inline handler to a `body`, which is the path a served runtime runs" — `lowerCallables` lowers INLINE functions; a post-build string `handler` resolved through the package's `functions` still runs in-process (hook-binder.ts), which is the path FAIL-2 below is about.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `runtime`, `objectql`, `cli`, `lint` — the five published packages the diff moves — with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` on the PR body and the changeset body alike; a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor`, so the level is right and no `!` is owed. Not breaking: a hook without `refusals` is answered byte-for-byte as before; the behaviour changes (a throw with no code or an undeclared code becoming a 500 fault; the body's `status` ignored) apply only to a hook that opts in by declaring a catalogue. No ADR-0087 marker is owed — `check-adr-0087-registration` reads breaking changesets only, and there is none. `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/app-shell` also move (published, same fixed group, root `.changeset/` per ui/AGENTS.md) and are not named in the changeset — the fixed group bumps them regardless, so this is a CHANGELOG omission, not a version error; `Check Changeset` is green. The `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — FILES` line is well-formed per the claim template (pm-dispatch SKILL.md: the seat files the owed card and rewrites it to `#N` before ACCEPT); the named eval file exists and has no `refusals` case.

### ③ Boundary flags

**FAIL-1 — the head's gate is red, and its tests are unmeasured.** `Lint · docs & code guards` failed on `78dc1452` (Error-code casing guard on `packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusals.test.ts:136`, `{ code: 'lower' }` as a fixture string), and every test/type-check shard was cancelled by the next push, so no test verdict exists for this head. The follow-up head `e5ea8881` carries the guard's own opt-out spelling for exactly that line and nothing else; it needs its own record, and FAIL-2 stands on it unchanged (the delta is one comment line).

**FAIL-2 — declared ≠ enforced on the in-process `handler` path.** `HookSchema` accepts `refusals` beside a `handler` (string or inline) with no `body`: `refuseUndeclaredLiteralRefusalCode` returns early (`body.language !== 'js'`), `hook-binder.ts` never reads `refusals`, and `resolveHookRefusal` runs only inside `hookBodyRunnerFactory`. For such a hook the save succeeds, `os i18n extract`/`check` demand one translation per entry and lint accepts the keys, yet the handler's throws are answered as before — the catalogue's message and status are never served and an undeclared code passes in silence, the card's defect wearing a declaration that promises otherwise. The ruling's "an undeclared code is refused loudly, at save where decidable" is decidable here: the pairing is visible to the schema. Remedy (either): a third-pair superRefine refusing `refusals` on a hook whose `body` is absent or not `js` (prescription: give the hook a sandboxed `body`, or drop `refusals`), with a pin in hook-refusals.test.ts; or wire the resolver into the in-process wrap in `hook-binder.ts` and record it in the liveness note. The PR body's "the in-process handler path is not covered (documented)" documents the hole; it does not close it.

Non-blocking, answered or escalated:
- **Open question (params).** Shipping plain-text messages is inside letter A. The later widening is additive only if the schema refuses double-brace holes in `message` now (or the platform commits to never interpolating a hook refusal); recommend the first in the follow-up card the dev proposes as option B.
- **Studio form gap.** Acceptable as a declared-but-unofferable key with an accurate ledger entry; the key-only record control follow-up is unfiled — the seat should file it or name the carrier in the ACCEPT.
- **Skills-docs follow-up.** `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json` has no `refusals` case and sits at its ceiling; the seat files the owed card and rewrites the line to `#N` before ACCEPT, per the claim template.
- **Liveness note over-claim** ("the build lowers an inline handler to a body, which is the path a served runtime runs"): true for inline functions, false for a post-build string `handler` — fix the sentence when FAIL-2 is closed, whichever remedy is taken.
- **Changeset coverage of `@object-ui/*`**: name `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/app-shell` in the changeset (patch-level entry lines) so their CHANGELOGs carry the group — or state in the PR why not; the version is correct either way.
- **Main drift**: merge `origin/main` (6 commits; translation.zod.ts region-disjoint) before the queue.
- Everything else the dev named as a deviation (buildSession, runtime wiring, ui lists, docs, fixture, counts, pins, ledger) is accepted as necessary; the `data-hooks.md` deletions that paid for the new section are accepted as true and within the ceiling.

I am not widening this PR with it. It belongs with the #26619 console half, or a one-line fix on main.
